To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the process of diffusion of the magnetic field into external layers of anisotropic magnetic core, the magnetic flux distribution over the cross section is distorted from the linear time dependence.
the slow diffusion of magnetic induction into external layers leads to the distortion from the linear dependence.
the magnetic flux in the cross section is not linearly dependent on time in the package with an anisotropic core.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the effective inductor systems for pulse power applications.
the effective inductor systems design for pulsed accelerations and actuators.
the optimization of the inductor system for the pulsed accelerator and actuator.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is effective for the improvement of inductor systems for the pulsed power technology.
the proposed approach allows to design effective magnetic field systems for pulsed magnetic accelerators and actuactors.
the simulation results of magnetic field distribution in the core with closed magnetic path at slow diffusion of field into external sheets are in good agreement with experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is important to take into account the magnetic field diffusion into the external sheets of package when designing inductive systems.
the simulation of magnetic flux evolution in anisotropic cores with closed magnetic path allows the prediction of the inductance value and the correction of magnetizing current pulse form.
the simulation of magnetic flux dynamics in anisotropic core package with a closed magnetic circuit is possible at linear rise of magnetic induction in time.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a closed magnetic circuit with an anisotropic magnetic core is a promising solution to the problem of creating an effective inductor system.
the linear rise of flux in time can be achieved by using a specially designed magnetizing force pulse.
it is possible to use an inductor of a pulsed accelerator or actuator with the magnetic field linearly rising in time.
